title: Concurrency in one screen
rememberThis: Task.Run and PLINQ are for CPU. I/O stays on async/await from module 13.
Never lock across Redis, HTTP, SQS, or RabbitMQ. The lock duration becomes your throughput ceiling.
On .NET 10 / C# 14, lock a dedicated System.Threading.Lock (C# 13+) or a private object. Never lock this, a Type, or a string.
volatile is not a lock. Prefer Interlocked or lock for shared counters and publication.
bullets: Monitor is what lock uses unless the target is System.Threading.Lock.
Mutex is cross-process; SemaphoreSlim is async-friendly throttling inside a process.
ConcurrentDictionary and Channel beat a locked List for producer/consumer.
Cache stampede at 999 users needs single-flight, not a lock around the Redis round-trip.
